title: Gong Alternatives for Real-Time Coaching
summary: Honest look at seven Gong alternatives for teams that want live in-call coaching, from Clari Copilot to Dialpad, with a comparison table and tradeoffs.
body_markdown:
Most teams searching for Gong alternatives are not unhappy with Gong. They want something it was never designed to do: help a rep while the call is still happening, when a hard question or an objection can still be answered.


## 01


Why do sales teams look beyond Gong?


Credit where it is due. Gong leads the conversation intelligence category. Its recording, deal analytics, and forecasting are the benchmark everyone else gets measured against, and most teams that buy it keep it.


The gap is timing. Conversation intelligence, as a category, works on recordings: the call ends, the system analyses it, and the insights arrive afterwards as scorecards, trackers, and deal warnings. That loop makes the next call better. It does nothing for the call in progress, where the rep faced a pricing objection alone and the manager only hears about it in Friday's review.


Real-time call guidance is the other half: software that listens during the call and surfaces help while the rep can still use it. The two categories complement each other more than they compete; we compare them in detail in[Conversation Intelligence vs Real-Time Call Guidance](https://www.caretta.so/blog/conversation-intelligence-vs-real-time) .


If live help is what sent you looking, judge the alternatives on that axis. Here is how the established options actually behave.


## 02


Which Gong alternatives coach reps during the call?


This list is scoped to teams that want live in-call coaching. Some well-known tools below do little or nothing live; we include them because they show up in every Gong comparison, and it is more useful to say plainly what each one does and does not do.


### 1. Clari Copilot


The closest established like-for-like for live coaching. Clari Copilot (formerly Wingman) shows battlecards during the call when it hears a trigger you set: a competitor name pulls up your counter-positioning, a pricing question pulls up your talk track. It also flags long monologues and poor talk ratios in the moment, and scores calls afterwards. It sits inside Clari's revenue platform, so it makes most sense if your forecasting lives there too. Honest limit: the cards are content someone on your team wrote and must keep current. The tool surfaces your prep; it does not generate an answer when the buyer asks something your cards never anticipated.


### 2. Avoma


Avoma covers the whole meeting lifecycle: scheduling, agendas, notes, transcription, and conversation intelligence, generally at a lower price point than Gong. Coaching happens after the call through scorecards and comment threads on recordings. During the call you get live transcription and bookmarks, which helps note-taking more than selling. A solid Gong replacement for smaller teams that mainly want notes and call review for less money. It will not talk a rep through an objection.


### 3. Salesloft


Salesloft is a sales engagement platform first: cadences, a dialler, email sequencing, and deal management, with call recording and analysis built in. If your team runs outreach through Salesloft already, its Conversations product can replace a standalone recorder and cut a line item. The live layer is thin, though; coaching arrives as post-call analysis inside the platform. Pick Salesloft when consolidating your outreach stack matters more than in-call help.


### 4. Dialpad


Dialpad is a business phone system with AI built in. On calls that run through its dialler it offers live transcription and real-time assist cards, and supervisors can watch active calls and step in. For phone-heavy inside sales or support teams that also need a comms platform, that is a genuinely live coaching setup from a large vendor. The limit is the walled garden: the assistance works inside Dialpad's own calls and meetings. If your team sells over Zoom or Google Meet with a different dialler, most of it does not apply. Its assist cards, like Clari's, fire on keywords against content you prepared.


### 5. Fathom


Fathom is an AI notetaker with a generous free tier: it records, transcribes, summarises, and pushes notes to your CRM. It does no coaching at all, live or afterwards, and does not pretend to. It earns its place here because a share of teams pricing Gong discover that what they actually need is reliable recording and notes at a fraction of the cost. If that is you, Fathom is the honest answer and the rest of this list is overkill.


### 6. Sybill


Sybill focuses on what happens after the call: summaries that read like a person wrote them, buyer sentiment and engagement cues from the video, drafted follow-up emails, and automatic CRM field updates. It gives reps hours of admin back and gives managers richer context than a transcript. Nothing happens during the call itself, so treat it as a post-call automation layer that matches Gong on notes quality while staying far lighter on analytics.


### 7. Caretta


The real-time option on this list. It listens to the live conversation and surfaces answers as the moment demands them: the right response to a security question, the proof point for a competitor claim, the handling for a pricing objection. The difference from battlecard tools is where the help comes from. Instead of firing pre-written cards on keywords, it draws on your company's docs, CRM, past calls, and the patterns of your best reps, so it can answer questions nobody scripted. It also preps the rep before the meeting and writes up notes after. It leaves revenue analytics alone; teams typically keep Gong for deal review and add the live layer on top. You can see how the live answering works on[the product page](https://www.caretta.so/product) .


## 03


How do these Gong alternatives compare?


Tool Coaches during the call? Best for Honest limit


Gong No; analysis after the call Revenue analytics and deal review at scale Feedback arrives after the moment has passed


Clari Copilot Yes; keyword-triggered battlecards Teams already on Clari Cards are hand-written and need upkeep


Avoma Barely; live transcript only Smaller teams wanting notes and CI for less Coaching is post-call scorecards


Salesloft No Consolidating outreach, dialler, and recording Thin live layer


Dialpad Yes, inside its own dialler Phone-heavy inside sales teams Little help on Zoom or Meet with another stack


Fathom No Cheap, reliable recording and notes No coaching of any kind


Sybill No Post-call notes, emails, CRM hygiene Nothing during the call


Caretta Yes; answers generated live from your knowledge Live answers and objection handling Does not replace revenue analytics


## 04


How should you choose?


Start from the moment you are trying to fix. If your problem is visibility into deals and rep performance, Gong is still the strongest tool on this page and you probably should not switch at all. If your problem is what happens inside the call, pick by stack: Clari Copilot if you are on Clari and your objections are predictable enough to script, Dialpad if your calls already run through its phone system, and a knowledge-driven live assistant if your reps face questions no battlecard deck can cover. We break the live options down by use case in[Best Real-Time AI Sales Assistants in 2026, by Use Case](https://www.caretta.so/blog/best-real-time-ai-sales-assistants) .


Whatever you pick, run it on real calls for a month before deciding. A tool that looks clever in a demo but distracts the rep mid-sentence is worse than no tool.
